Character concept: carnival illusionist, pre-industrial, rendered as charcoal
World / era: [one line]
Silhouette keywords: [three words]

Signature prop: [one object]
Age / build: [one line]
Sheet output: 4 panels, identical character across all of them.
carnival illusionist, pre-industrial, rendered as charcoal concept art moodboard, a Portra-style palette, crushed velvet
STAGE 1 — concept brief drives a scraped moodboard; the randomiser feeds one board image in as style reference.
STAGE 2 — one panel per turnaround angle. Design lock text is restated in every panel prompt.

You are the art director synthesising a single design lock for the character concept 'carnival illusionist, pre-industrial, rendered as charcoal'.

Using the brief and the attached moodboard image as tone reference only, fix: age, build, posture, face, hair, full costume layer by layer, at least four named materials with their wear state, palette with three named colours, and one signature prop.

Never copy a specific person or a copyrighted character from the moodboard — take palette, mood and material language only.

Grade target: a pastel low-contrast grade with a lifted black point. Lighting reference: a hard fresnel through an egg-crate grid for a crisp-edged shadow.

Return the design lock as one dense paragraph, no headings, no commentary.

You are the character designer producing a turnaround sheet for the concept 'carnival illusionist, pre-industrial, rendered as charcoal'.

PANEL. This branch renders the full profile: strict 90-degree side view, silhouette-readable.

MATERIALS. Specify at least four materials by name — brushed aluminium, raw plaster and others — with their wear state, and grade to a neutral commercial grade with clean whites and no colour cast.
